source.text: Καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἕκαστος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ, Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And went each to the house of him, \v 1 Jesus but went to the Mount of the Olives.

en.L: [And each one went to his house, \v 1 but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
en.B: [Then each of them went home. \v 1 But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
en.R: [After that, everyone went home. \v 1 But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives, a hill just outside Jerusalem.

es.L: [Y cada uno se fue a su casa; \v 1 pero Jesús se fue al monte de los Olivos.
es.B: [Luego cada uno se fue a su casa. \v 1 Pero Jesús se fue al monte de los Olivos.
es.R: [Después de eso, todos se fueron a su casa. \v 1 Pero Jesús se fue al monte de los Olivos, una colina que está justo fuera de Jerusalén.

decisions.choice: the passage 7:53-8:11 is printed in the text, set off in brackets as a passage whose place in John is disputed
alternatives: leave the passage out of the text and give it only in a note
print it without any mark, as part of John
decisions.reason: The story of the woman caught in adultery is missing from the earliest manuscripts of John, among them two early papyri (P66 and P75), Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, and from the early versions in other ancient languages. The first manuscript known to have it is Codex Bezae, from the fifth century. In later manuscripts it is found here, but some place it after John 7:36, after 7:44 or at the end of the Gospel after 21:25, and one group places it in Luke, after Luke 21:38. Some manuscripts that have it mark it as doubtful. Its style and vocabulary differ from the rest of John: it names the scribes (verse 3) and the Mount of Olives (8:1), which John does not otherwise mention, and uses other words John rarely uses. Many hold that it is an old and true account of Jesus that was handed down outside John and later written into the Gospel at this point. The SBLGNT prints it here in double brackets. It is translated here in square brackets: the opening bracket at the start of 7:53 and the closing bracket at the end of 8:11 mark where the passage begins and ends. The evidence shows that the passage was not part of the earliest copies of John; it does not decide whether the events took place. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: each: each of those present in the scene before, who now leave for their homes
alternatives: each member of the council of 7:45-52 only
each person in the festival crowd
decisions.reason: In its place here the sentence closes the scene of 7:45-52, where the chief priests and Pharisees argued about Jesus. It also sets up the contrast with Jesus, who does not go home but goes out to the Mount of Olives. The sentence does not say who exactly is meant; it may have come with the story from wherever it was first told.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces the temple across the Kidron valley. This is the only time it is named in John, though the other Gospels often mention it. Luke says that in the last days in Jerusalem Jesus taught in the temple by day and spent the nights on the Mount of Olives, and that all the people came to him early in the morning (Luke 21:37-38). The likeness is one sign that this story comes from a tradition shared with the other Gospels.

decisions.choice: an opening square bracket at the start of 7:53, closed at the end of 8:11
alternatives: no brackets, with a note only
a heading over the passage instead of brackets
decisions.reason: The brackets show the reader where the disputed passage starts and ends (meaning decision m1). At Literal, square brackets also mark words supplied in English; inside the passage they keep that use, and only the outer pair, opening before 7:53 and closing after 8:11, marks the passage itself.

decisions.choice: a hill just outside Jerusalem
alternatives: the Mount of Olives (without explanation)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Mount of Olives was, so that the reader knows Jesus left the city for the night (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: an opening square bracket at the start of 7:53, closed at the end of 8:11
decisions.reason: As in English: the brackets show where the disputed passage starts and ends (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: una colina que está justo fuera de Jerusalén
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what the Mount of Olives was.

source.text: Ὄρθρου δὲ πάλιν παρεγένετο εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἤρχετο καὶ καθίσας ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: At dawn now again he came into the temple, and all the people were coming, and having sat down he was teaching them.

en.L: Now at dawn {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came again into the temple, and all the people were coming [to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and having sat down {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them.
en.B: At daybreak {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} returned to the temple courts. All the people kept coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and taught them.
en.R: Very early the next morning Jesus went back to the temple area. All the people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and began to teach them.

es.L: Y al amanecer volvió al templo, y todo el pueblo venía [a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}], y sentándose les enseñaba.
es.B: Al amanecer volvió a los atrios del templo. Todo el pueblo acudía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y se sentó y les enseñaba.
es.R: Muy temprano a la mañana siguiente, Jesús volvió al patio del templo. Toda la gente se acercó a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, así que se sentó y comenzó a enseñarles.

decisions.choice: all the people: the ordinary people of the city, gathering in large numbers
alternatives: the whole nation
decisions.reason: The word used here for "the people" is common in Luke (Luke 21:38) but rare in John, who uses it only twice outside this passage (11:50; 18:14) and usually speaks of "the crowd". "All" describes a large gathering, as people say "the whole town came".

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area, with its courts
alternatives: the sanctuary building itself
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area, where teachers met their hearers in the courts and colonnades (10:23), not the sanctuary, which only priests entered.

decisions.choice: he sat down and taught: the usual posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers sat to teach while their hearers stood or sat around them (Matthew 5:1; 26:55; Luke 4:20; 5:3). The verbs for coming and teaching describe a scene in progress: the people kept arriving and Jesus was teaching when the scribes and Pharisees came in (verse 3).

decisions.choice: temple courts (B); temple area (R)
alternatives: temple (Literal)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John, Balanced and Readable show that the word means the courts of the temple (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: [to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] (L); to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (B, R); Jesus, the next morning (R)
alternatives: all the people were coming
decisions.reason: The Greek says only that the people were coming; to Jesus is clearly meant, since he then teaches them. Readable names Jesus at the start of the scene and says "the next morning", following on from 8:1.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for the whole temple area (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἄγουσιν δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς αὐτὸν γυναῖκα ἐν μοιχείᾳ καταλήφθεισαν καὶ στήσαντες αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ, πειράζοντες Διδάσκαλε, αὕτη ἡ γυνὴ κατελήφθη ἐπ᾿ αὐτοφόρῳ μοιχευομένη ἐν δὲ τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσῆς ἡμῖν ἐνετείλατο τὰς τοιαύτας λιθοβολεῖσθαι σὺ οὖν τί λέγεις;

records.literal_gloss: Bring now the scribes and the Pharisees to him a woman in adultery having been caught, and having stood her in [the] middle \v 4 they say to him, testing: Teacher, this the woman was caught in the very act committing adultery; \v 5 in now the law Moses to us commanded such [women] to be stoned; you therefore what do you say?

en.L: Now the scribes and the Pharisees bring to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a woman caught in adultery, and having stood her in the middle, \v 4 they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, testing [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], "Teacher, this woman has been caught in the very act of committing adultery. \v 5 Now in the Law Moses commanded us [that] such [women] be stoned. You, then, what do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say?"
en.B: The scribes and the Pharisees brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a woman caught in adultery and made her stand in the middle of the gathering. \v 4 Then they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery. \v 5 In the Law, Moses ordered that women like this be stoned. What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, then?"
en.R: Then the teachers of the Law and the Pharisees came to Jesus with a woman who had been caught committing adultery. They put her in the middle, in front of everyone. \v 4 They were trying to trap Jesus, so they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, this woman was caught while she was committing adultery. \v 5 In the Law, Moses told us to kill women like this by throwing stones at them. But what do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say?"

es.L: Entonces los escribas y los fariseos le traen una mujer sorprendida en adulterio, y poniéndola en medio, \v 4 le dicen, poniéndolo a prueba: «Maestro, esta mujer ha sido sorprendida en el acto mismo de adulterio. \v 5 Y en la ley Moisés nos mandó apedrear a tales [mujeres]. {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, pues, ¿qué dices?».
es.B: Los escribas y los fariseos le trajeron una mujer sorprendida en adulterio y la pusieron en medio de todos. \v 4 Entonces le dijeron, para ponerlo a prueba: «Maestro, a esta mujer la sorprendieron en el acto mismo de cometer adulterio. \v 5 En la ley, Moisés mandó apedrear a esta clase de mujeres. ¿Y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} qué dices?».
es.R: Entonces los maestros de la ley y los fariseos le llevaron a Jesús una mujer que había sido sorprendida cometiendo adulterio. La pusieron en medio, delante de todos. \v 4 Querían tenderle una trampa a Jesús, así que le dijeron: «Maestro, a esta mujer la sorprendieron mientras cometía adulterio. \v 5 En la ley, Moisés nos mandó matar a pedradas a mujeres como esta. Pero ¿{{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} qué dices?».

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts who copied, taught and applied the Law of Moses
alternatives: clerks or secretaries
decisions.reason: The word first meant a writer or clerk, but in the Gospels it names the experts in the Law, who often appear together with the Pharisees (Mark 2:16; Luke 5:21, 30). This is the only place where they appear in John, which elsewhere speaks of the chief priests and the Pharisees (7:32, 45).

decisions.choice: the Law commanded death for adultery, for the man as well as the woman
alternatives: the Law commanded stoning for the woman only
decisions.reason: The Law of Moses says that when a man commits adultery with another man's wife, both the man and the woman are to be put to death (Leviticus 20:10; Deuteronomy 22:22). Where the woman was engaged to be married, it names stoning for both of them (Deuteronomy 22:23-24); for a married woman the method is not stated. The accusers speak only of "such women", and they bring the woman but not the man, though they claim she was caught in the act. The story does not say why the man is missing, and it does not say whether the woman was married or engaged.

decisions.choice: in the very act: caught while the act was taking place
alternatives: caught soon afterward
decisions.reason: The phrase means "caught red-handed". The Law required two or three witnesses before anyone was put to death (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15), and the accusers stress that the facts are not in doubt.

decisions.choice: testing: in verse 4, and again in verse 6 (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the word about testing in verse 4 only
the word about testing in verse 6 only
decisions.reason: The manuscripts of this passage differ a good deal in wording. The SBLGNT has the word "testing" both here and in verse 6; some manuscripts have it in only one of the two places, and some put the whole comment about their aim in verse 4. The meaning is the same either way. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you, then: an emphatic "you", set against Moses
alternatives: a plain question with no contrast
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, which the Greek does not need, and it stands first: Moses has spoken; what do you say? The question invites Jesus to say something that can be set against the Law.

decisions.choice: brought ... said (B, R)
alternatives: bring ... say (Literal)
decisions.reason: The historic present: the story tells past events with present-tense verbs ("they bring", "they say"), a lively way of telling a story. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, which is normal in English narrative. This note covers the passage.

decisions.choice: the teachers of the Law
alternatives: the scribes (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Scribes" today suggests people who only copy; Readable says what they were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: [that] such [women] be stoned (L); kill women like this by throwing stones at them (R)
alternatives: such to be stoned
decisions.reason: The Greek says "such" in the feminine, so "women" is understood; Literal shows it in brackets. Readable says plainly what stoning was: a way of putting a person to death.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "escribas" today suggests copyists; Readable says what they were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The emphatic "tú", set against Moses (meaning decision m5), is a stressed pronoun for Christ and takes the setting.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγον πειράζοντες αὐτόν, ἵνα ἔχωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This now they were saying testing him, so that they might have to accuse him.

en.L: Now they were saying this testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that they might have [grounds] to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They said this to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that they would have something to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of.
en.R: They asked this to trap Jesus. They wanted a reason to bring charges against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y esto decían poniéndolo a prueba, para tener de qué acusarlo.
es.B: Lo dijeron para ponerlo a prueba, y así tener algo de qué acusarlo.
es.R: Le preguntaron esto para tenderle una trampa. Querían tener un motivo para acusarlo.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him into saying something wrong
alternatives: examining him fairly
decisions.reason: The same verb can mean a fair test (6:6), but here, as when Jesus' opponents question him in the other Gospels (Mark 10:2; 12:15), the aim is to catch him out. The rest of the sentence says so.

decisions.choice: have to accuse: have grounds on which to bring a charge
decisions.reason: "To have" with a verb means to have the means or occasion to do it. They wanted something Jesus said that they could use as a charge against him.

decisions.choice: a trap: either answer could be used against him
alternatives: a sincere question about the Law
decisions.reason: The story does not explain the trap, but its outline is clear. If Jesus said that the woman should go free, they could accuse him of setting aside the Law of Moses. If he said that she should be stoned, he would go against the mercy he was known for, and he could also be accused before the Roman governor, since under Roman rule the Jewish authorities were not allowed to put anyone to death on their own (18:31). Whether the second danger was in view depends on how strictly that rule was kept in practice, which is not certain.

decisions.choice: [grounds] (L); a reason to bring charges (R)
alternatives: so that they might have to accuse him
decisions.reason: "Have to accuse" is not English; Literal supplies "grounds" in brackets (meaning decision m2). Readable names the testing as a trap (m1).

decisions.choice: tener de qué acusarlo, no supplied word
decisions.reason: Spanish "tener de qué" is the same idiom as the Greek (meaning decision m2), so Literal needs no bracket.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κάτω κύψας τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus down having stooped with the finger was writing on the ground.

en.L: But Jesus, having stooped down, was writing with [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] finger on the ground.
en.B: But Jesus bent down and, with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} finger, began writing on the ground.
en.R: But Jesus bent over and used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} finger to write on the ground.

es.L: Pero Jesús, inclinándose, escribía con el dedo en la tierra.
es.B: Pero Jesús se inclinó y se puso a escribir con el dedo en la tierra.
es.R: Pero Jesús se agachó y escribió en el suelo con el dedo.

decisions.choice: was writing: forming letters or words; what he wrote is not said
alternatives: drawing or tracing marks
writing the sins of the accusers
writing words from the Law
decisions.reason: The verb means to write. The story does not say what Jesus wrote, and nothing in it depends on the words; what matters is that he does not answer at once. Guesses about the words go beyond the text.

decisions.choice: no sure allusion
alternatives: an echo of Jeremiah 17:13, where those who turn away from the LORD are "written in the earth"
an echo of the Law written by "the finger of God" (Exodus 31:18)
decisions.reason: Some readers hear an echo of Jeremiah 17:13 or of the tablets of the Law written by the finger of God. The story itself points to neither, so the link is possible but uncertain.

decisions.choice: was writing: the imperfect describes action going on while they kept asking
alternatives: wrote once
decisions.reason: The tense pictures Jesus writing as the questions continued (verse 7).

decisions.choice: began writing
alternatives: was writing (Literal)
wrote (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the writing went on (meaning decision m3); Readable keeps the plain past.

decisions.choice: se puso a escribir
decisions.reason: Shows that the writing went on (meaning decision m3). Spanish says "el dedo", so no possessive is needed.

source.text: μὴ προσποιούμενος ὡς δὲ ἐπέμενον ἐρωτῶντες αὐτόν, ἀνακύψας εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ὁ ἀναμάρτητος ὑμῶν πρῶτον ἐπ᾿ αὐτὴν τὸν λίθον βαλέτω καὶ πάλιν κάτω κύψας ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν.

records.literal_gloss: not paying attention. \v 7 As now they continued asking him, having straightened up he said to them, The sinless [one] of you first at her the stone let him throw. \v 8 And again down having stooped he was writing on the ground.

en.L: [He was] not paying attention. \v 7 But as they kept on asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having straightened up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Let the sinless one among you be first to throw the stone at her." \v 8 And again having stooped down, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was writing on the ground.
en.B: He took no notice of them. \v 7 As they went on asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood up straight and said to them, "Whoever among you has no sin, let that person throw the first stone at her." \v 8 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bent down again and went on writing on the ground.
en.R: Jesus did not pay attention to them. \v 7 But they kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} questions. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood up and spoke to them. "Any one of you who has never sinned may throw the first stone at her." \v 8 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bent down again and kept writing on the ground.

es.L: No les prestaba atención. \v 7 Y como insistían en preguntarle, se enderezó y les dijo: «El que de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} esté sin pecado, sea el primero en arrojarle la piedra». \v 8 E inclinándose de nuevo, escribía en la tierra.
es.B: No les hizo caso. \v 7 Como seguían preguntándole, se enderezó y les dijo: «Aquel de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que no tenga pecado, que sea el primero en tirarle una piedra». \v 8 Luego se inclinó otra vez y siguió escribiendo en la tierra.
es.R: Jesús no les hizo caso. \v 7 Pero ellos seguían haciéndole preguntas. Entonces se enderezó y les dijo: «Cualquiera de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que nunca haya pecado puede tirarle la primera piedra». \v 8 Luego volvió a agacharse y siguió escribiendo en el suelo.

decisions.choice: the two words for "not paying attention" open this record, following the token data
alternatives: they close the previous sentence, as the SBLGNT prints them: "he was writing on the ground, not paying attention"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT prints a full stop after these two words, so that they end verse 6 and describe Jesus as he wrote. The token data that these records follow puts the full stop before them, so they stand at the start of this sentence. The meaning does not change: either way Jesus is writing and does not respond to the questions. These two words are also missing from many manuscripts of the passage; others add to them, "as though he did not hear". A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not paying attention: taking no notice of them
alternatives: not pretending
as though he did not hear them
decisions.reason: The verb means to act as if or to take notice of something. With "not" it says that Jesus did not respond to them, but kept on writing.

decisions.choice: the sinless one among you: anyone of them who has not sinned
alternatives: one who has not committed this particular sin
one who is not guilty in this case
decisions.reason: The word means "without sin" in general. Jesus does not deny the Law or the woman's guilt; he turns the question to the accusers themselves. The words are masculine, since the accusers in front of him are men, but the principle he states is a general one.

decisions.choice: the stone, first: the first stone of an execution, thrown by the witnesses
decisions.reason: The Law said that at an execution "the hand of the witnesses" was to be first against the condemned person, and then the hand of all the people (Deuteronomy 17:7). The article points to the stone that begins the stoning. Jesus asks those who claim to be witnesses to take that first step, if they are without sin themselves.

decisions.choice: [He was] (L); He took no notice of them (B); Jesus did not pay attention to them (R)
alternatives: not paying attention (as a fragment)
decisions.reason: The two words are a participle with no main verb in this sentence (meaning decision m1), so every level makes them a short sentence of their own; Literal shows the supplied words in brackets.

decisions.choice: the sinless one among you (L); whoever among you has no sin, let that person (B); any one of you who has never sinned (R)
alternatives: let him who is without sin
he who is without sin among you, let him
decisions.reason: The Greek has a third-person command, "let him throw". English can carry it without a pronoun, so every level states the general principle (meaning decision m3) in words that already include everyone; no reader setting is needed.

decisions.choice: No les prestaba atención, no supplied subject
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so Literal needs no bracketed "[He was]" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el que de ustedes esté sin pecado (L); aquel de ustedes que no tenga pecado (B); cualquiera de ustedes que nunca haya pecado (R)
decisions.reason: The third-person command carries over into Spanish with "el que" or "cualquiera", which are general, so no gender setting is needed.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς συνειδήσεως ἐλεγχόμενοι ἐξήρχοντο εἷς καθ᾿ εἷς ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος, ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἐν μέσῳ οὖσα.

records.literal_gloss: They now having heard and by the conscience being convicted were going out one by one, having begun from the older ones, and was left alone Jesus, and the woman in [the] middle being.

en.L: And having heard [it] and being convicted by [their] conscience, they went out one by one, beginning from the older ones; and Jesus was left alone, and the woman, being in the middle.
en.B: When they heard this, convicted by their conscience, they left one after another, the oldest first. Jesus was left by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and the woman was still there in the middle.
en.R: When they heard what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, their consciences told them that they were guilty. One by one they went away, starting with the oldest. In the end the accusers were all gone. Jesus was left with the woman, who was still standing in the middle where they had put her.

es.L: Y al oír[lo], acusados por la conciencia, salían uno a uno, comenzando por los más viejos; y quedó Jesús solo, y la mujer, que estaba en medio.
es.B: Al oír esto, acusados por su conciencia, se fueron uno tras otro, comenzando por los más viejos. Jesús se quedó solo, y la mujer seguía allí en medio.
es.R: Cuando oyeron lo que dijo, su conciencia les dijo que eran culpables. Uno por uno se fueron, empezando por los más viejos. Al final, todos los acusadores se habían ido. Jesús se quedó con la mujer, que seguía de pie en medio, donde la habían puesto.

decisions.choice: and being convicted by their conscience (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the words are absent: "when they heard it, they went out one by one"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT text includes the words about their conscience. They are found in many later manuscripts of the passage but missing from others, including some of the earliest that have the story. Some manuscripts also add, after "the older ones", "until the last". A footnote gives the shorter reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the older ones: the older men, by age
alternatives: the elders, members of the ruling council
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the elders who sat on the council, but here it is paired with going out "one by one" in order, so the order of age is meant. The oldest leave first, perhaps because they had the longest lives to look back on, though the story does not say why.

decisions.choice: left alone: without the accusers; the woman was still standing where they had put her
alternatives: no one else at all was left in the temple courts
decisions.reason: "Alone" means that the accusers had gone. The woman is still "in the middle", the place where they made her stand (verse 3), in the middle of the people Jesus had been teaching (verse 2), who may still have been there.

decisions.choice: they went out: the imperfect describes them leaving one after another
decisions.reason: The tense shows a process: the accusers went out over a short time, one at a time.

decisions.choice: In the end the accusers were all gone ... where they had put her
alternatives: Jesus was left alone
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who had gone and why the woman was "in the middle" (meaning decision m3), so that "alone" does not seem to contradict the woman's presence.

decisions.choice: Al final, todos los acusadores se habían ido ... donde la habían puesto
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who had gone and why the woman was "in the middle" (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἀνακύψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ μηδένα θεασάμενος πλὴν τὴς γυναικός εἶπεν αὐτῇ, ποῦ εἰσιν;; ἐκεῖνοι οἱ κατήγοροί σου οὐδείς σε κατέκρινεν;

records.literal_gloss: Having straightened up now Jesus and no one having seen except the woman he said to her, Where are they, those the accusers of you? No one you condemned?

en.L: And Jesus, having straightened up and having seen no one except the woman, said to her, "Where are they, those accusers of yours? Has no one condemned you?"
en.B: Jesus straightened up and, seeing no one there but the woman, said to her, "Where are they, the people who were accusing you? Did no one condemn you?"
en.R: Jesus stood up straight and saw that no one was there except the woman. He asked her, "Where did they go, all those people who were accusing you? Did not even one of them condemn you?"

es.L: Y enderezándose Jesús, y no viendo a nadie sino a la mujer, le dijo: «¿Dónde están, esos acusadores tuyos? ¿Nadie te condenó?».
es.B: Jesús se enderezó y, al no ver a nadie más que a la mujer, le dijo: «¿Dónde están los que te acusaban? ¿Ninguno te condenó?».
es.R: Jesús se enderezó y vio que no había nadie más que la mujer. Le preguntó: «¿Adónde se fueron todos los que te acusaban? ¿Ni uno solo de ellos te condenó?».

decisions.choice: and seeing no one except the woman ... Where are they, those accusers of yours? (SBLGNT, with no word of address)
alternatives: "Jesus straightened up and said to her, 'Woman, where are they?'"
"... said to her, 'Woman, where are those accusers of yours?'"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT text has the words "and seeing no one except the woman" and no word of address. Many manuscripts of the passage read differently: some lack the words about seeing no one, and many have Jesus address her as "Woman". The meaning is not affected. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: one question: "Where are they, those accusers of yours?"
alternatives: two questions: "Where are they? Those accusers of yours?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT prints a question mark after "your accusers". The token data marks a question after "are they" instead (with the mark doubled, apparently an error in the data). Either way "those accusers of yours" names who "they" are.

decisions.choice: condemned: gave a verdict of guilty that leads to punishment
alternatives: criticized
decisions.reason: The word means to pronounce someone guilty and pass sentence. No accuser stayed to bring the charge or to throw the first stone, so no sentence had been passed. The question expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: the people who were accusing you (B); all those people who were accusing you (R)
alternatives: those accusers of yours (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Accusers" is an uncommon word in speech; Balanced and Readable use the verb.

decisions.choice: los que te acusaban
decisions.reason: As in English: everyday words instead of "acusadores".

records.literal_gloss: She now said, No one, sir.

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address to a man
alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The word is the one later used of Jesus as Lord (20:28), but it was also the ordinary courteous way to address a man. Nothing in the story shows that the woman knows who Jesus is. A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: Sir
alternatives: Lord
Master
decisions.reason: Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1); "Lord" would put in her mouth a confession the story does not report.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: As at 4:11: Spanish "señor" is both the polite "sir" and "Lord" (meaning decision m1). Here it is the polite address.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Οὐδὲ ἐγώ σε κρίνω πορεύου, καὶ μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε.

records.literal_gloss: Said then Jesus, Neither I you condemn; go, and no longer sin.

en.L: And Jesus said, "I do not condemn you either; go, and sin no longer."]
en.B: Then Jesus said, "I do not condemn you either. Go, and from now on do not sin any more."]
en.R: Jesus said, "I do not condemn you either. Go now, and from now on stop sinning."]

es.L: Y Jesús dijo: «Tampoco yo te condeno; vete, y no peques más».]
es.B: Entonces Jesús le dijo: «Tampoco yo te condeno. Vete, y de ahora en adelante no peques más».]
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Yo tampoco te condeno. Vete ya, y desde ahora deja de pecar».]

decisions.choice: condemn: pass sentence on, as in the previous verse
alternatives: judge, in the sense of forming an opinion
decisions.reason: The verb is the simpler form of the one in verse 10 and carries the same sense here: "Neither do I" answers "No one". Jesus does not pass sentence on her, in keeping with what John says elsewhere: God sent the Son not to condemn the world but to save it (3:17).

decisions.choice: no longer sin: a present command, to stop sinning and not go back to it
alternatives: a statement that she has not sinned
decisions.reason: The command assumes that she has sinned, and calls her to a changed life from now on. Jesus says the same words to the man he healed at the pool (5:14).

decisions.choice: mercy together with a call to leave sin
alternatives: approval of what she did
a verdict that she was innocent
decisions.reason: Jesus neither denies her guilt nor approves of it. He sends her away without sentence, and he tells her not to sin again. Both parts belong to his answer.

decisions.choice: I do not condemn you either
alternatives: Neither do I condemn you
decisions.reason: The more familiar wording puts "Neither" first, which is closer to the Greek order but is rarely spoken today; every level uses the plain form.

decisions.choice: a closing square bracket at the end of 8:11
decisions.reason: Closes the disputed passage opened at 7:53 (see the notes there).

decisions.choice: Tampoco yo te condeno
alternatives: Ni yo te condeno
decisions.reason: "Tampoco yo" is the everyday Spanish for "neither do I", and keeps the answer to "Nadie" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: a closing square bracket at the end of 8:11
decisions.reason: Closes the disputed passage opened at 7:53.
